description: Fetch the exact, in-force text of one specific article by number from a named Romanian law or code (e.g. article 291 of 'codul fiscal', article 5 of 'codul penal'). Use this when you need a precise article verbatim, with its citation. Amendment history is returned separately under '— Modificări —', not mixed into the text. Set `paragraph` to fetch just one alineat (e.g. "1" → alin. (1)) instead of the whole article; a whole citation written into `article` ("7 alin. (19)", "art. 169 alin. (1) lit. d)", several letters at once: "art. 291 alin. (2) lit. a) și c)" or "lit. a)-c)") is read correctly too. An act with no articles — the norms of a code (law="normele de aplicare a Codului fiscal"), an instruction, a procedure — is made of numbered POINTS: pass `article` as "Titlul II pct. 3", "pct. 3.1" or "Anexa nr. 2 pct. 1"; a bare "291" returns the points that CITE art. 291 of the code. Returns the IN-FORCE version; to read it as it stood on a past date pass `date` (the same result as lookup_article_at_date); for repealed/old law pass `include_repealed: true` (the same as lookup_article_historical).

date.description: Optional. YYYY-MM-DD: read the article as it stood on that date instead of today. The same as lookup_article_at_date.

include_repealed.description: Optional. true: look in repealed / old law too (e.g. the old Cod fiscal, Legea 571/2003). The same as lookup_article_historical. With `date` as well, the dated read wins: it never drops a date.

law.description: The act, however it is at hand: a citation ('Legea 265/2022', 'HG 1/2016', 'Ordinul 2594/C/2008'), a common name ('Codul fiscal'), a title any tool printed, or 'normele de aplicare a Legii X'.

paragraph.description: Optional. One alineat to return, e.g. "1" or "1^1" — scopes the result to that paragraph and its litere/puncte, reducing noise.

point.description: Optional. One point (pct.) to return, e.g. "42". Use this on definitions articles, where every point sits under a SINGLE alineat so `paragraph` returns the whole article. A large article comes back as a structure map listing its points — pass one of those ids here.

summary.description: Optional. true: the structure of the article (its alineate, points or letters with their opening words and figures) and its first alineat in full, whatever its size. Today's text only.

name: lookup_article
